chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to me, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, saying: Abu Abdullah al-Razi narrated to me, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Uthman, from Ahmad ibn Umar al-Hallal, from Yahya ibn Imran al-Halabi, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) say:

The proud should not expect good praise, nor the imposter many friends, nor the ill-mannered honor, nor the miser kinship ties, nor the mocker of people sincere affection, nor the one with little jurisprudence judgment, nor the backbiter safety, nor the jealous one heart's ease, nor the one who punishes for a small sin mastery/prestige, nor the inexperienced one who is pleased with his own opinion leadership.
ai.seo_question: What are the ten pairs of character flaws and unfulfilled expectations mentioned in al-Khisal?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Khisal*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the intrinsic link between internal character traits and external social or spiritual rewards, emphasizing that merit is not merely claimed but earned through consistency. This teaching reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on *adab* (etiquette) and *fiqh* (jurisprudence) as prerequisites for leadership and social harmony, warning against the hypocrisy of expecting honor without the corresponding virtue. It serves as a practical guide for self-assessment, ensuring that one's aspirations align with their actual moral and intellectual state.
